name: overgrown wild shrub: dense leafy bush clumps in several greens with a few dry twigs
label: wasteland_ruins/bush-wild

surfaces.part: leafy shrub mound, upper dome with lighter leaf clumps
front foliage mass with a dark shadowed base
dry twigs at upper right and left

answer.evidence: The shrub is a rounded foliage mound that widens from 5 px at row 0 to 32 px at rows 17-24, then narrows to 27 px at row 27 and 17 px at row 28. It has no hard edge line and no ellipse. The lighter leaf clumps in rows 1-13 read as the upper surface of a heap seen from above (evidence d), and the darker rows 14-28 with a shadowed base at rows 26-28 form the front face. The top reading is weak because the shading is organic and nothing marks a clear boundary between top and front. The twigs are decor.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small dark bush with roughly 5 green steps, built from clumped leaf shapes with a small dry twig at the upper right. Its 8 visible tones per tile are above the same-scale reference tree-1a786c (7), and its near-flat coverage is 0%, so there are no flat fills. The dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, and by eye the outline is a dark green that leans toward the leaf colour, not a black sticker line. It falls short of the references in contrast: the highlight end of the ramp is compressed, so the bush reads as a slightly muted mass with fewer bright leaf clumps than tree-1a786c. It is still comparable to tree-1a786c in structure and tone count. It is nowhere near the richness of tree-d43edd (29 tones), but that is a much larger piece. A careful artist would accept it as a small shrub next to tree-1a786c.

answer.evidence: The silhouette is a domed mound that widens steadily from 5 px at row 0 to 32 px at rows 17-24, then rounds off at the bottom. In column x=16, rows 1-13 are lighter foliage, which reads as the canopy seen from above. A dark pixel at row 10 acts as a weak edge line. Rows 14-26 are darker and form the front mass, and rows 26-28 are dark base shadow. The top/front split is soft and there is no crisp edge line, so this is a judgement call, but the lighter upper canopy over a darker 13-row front mass reads as a 3/4 mound rather than a flat elevation.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small dark-green bush with a couple of twigs. By eye, though, the canopy reads as a low-contrast, dark blob with only about 4 distinct green steps. Leaf clumps lack the bright highlights and the individual leaf scallops of the references. The "several greens" in the brief and the clump definition are weak, and the bush is much flatter and more muted than either reference, which show 5-6 clear lightness steps and crisp leaf-cluster highlights. The few dry twigs are barely visible, one at the top right. It is not flat-filled, but a careful artist would see it as thinner and less textured next to the references, and the d43edd reference is far richer.
